root_cause: The datepicker component updates the input value to a locale-specific string during initialization when the input has a value, causing the submitted departure date to change from ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD) to locale format (MM/DD/YYYY) even when the user cancels the date picker without selecting a date.
repair_strategy: Remove the call to _updateDisplayWithSelectedDates in _initCalendar to prevent the input value from being updated during initialization. The _parseInputValue method already sets the calendar's internal state from the input value without updating the input, so removing the subsequent call preserves the input's original value.
expected_accessibility_effect: Users can now cancel the date picker without altering the input value, preserving the initially set ISO format date for form submission. Keyboard-only users retain expected behavior when dismissing the date picker with Escape.
functional_risks: If the input value is invalid or not a date, the calendar will not show a selected date (same as before).
Programmatic date setting via setSelectedDates will still update the input as expected.
Inline datepickers are unaffected as they skip the removed logic.
The visual representation of the date in the input will remain in ISO format until a date is selected, which may deviate from locale expectations but matches the initial value.
verification_requirements: Verify that focusing the departure input does not change its value.
Verify that pressing Escape after focusing the departure input leaves the value unchanged.
Verify that submitting the form after changing only the passengers field sends the departure value in ISO format.
Verify that selecting a date from the date picker updates the input to the locale-specific format (if locale is set) or ISO format (if no locale formatting is configured).
Verify that inline datepickers continue to function correctly.
